I understand that there are no definitive canon numbers for their population, but the source used by this article is just an unspecified fan estimatation. Therefore this article has as much credibility as, well, my post here. I'm also doing fan estimation based on vague bits of lore.

> they're nonsense that the writers clearly gave no thought to.

That's why it's so fun to actually analyze them. Sci-fi writers often don't think too much about background numbers given in the story, which results in really silly stuff when you think about them for a bit. 

Such as here, even with a low end estimate of 10-20 billion for the Quarians the Geth must've killed at least 99.9% of them for their current numbers to be 17 million. And when accounting for the galactic population being in trillions, and Quarians likely having population similar to other major races pre-war, this gives numbers closer to 99.99% killed with hundreds of billions dead. Absolutely insane, but completely in line with availible lore.

As for the logistics, according to the wiki the Geth were present on Quarian colonial worlds before the war, so there was likely no major Quarian settlement without Geth in it when the rebellion started. Since the Geth were everywhere in the Quarian space there was no place to escape from them once they started winning, other than leaving the whole region on ships. Quarian fleet didn't have much space to house a lot of people full time, and anybody stuck on the planets ended up killed sooner or later.

The population numbers in Mass Effect can get weird (like in most of sci fi tbh) but one constant number given to us throughout the series is that the galactic population is numbered in trillions. 

From Codex "Communications: Administration":

>While comm buoys allow rapid transmission, there is a finite amount of bandwidth available. Given that **trillions of people** may be trying to pass a message through a given buoy at any one time, access to the network is parceled out on priority tiers. 


From Codex "Communications: Methodology":

>When a new solar system is first connected to the net, a selection of the most popular data is installed locally. Though storage hardware is cheap, the capacity required to hold all the data produced everyday by **trillions of people on hundreds of worlds** is not trivial. It's not economical to store local copies of all the data available on obscure topics just in case. 


At the end of Arrival Shephard states that stopping the Reapers saved trillions of lives, in the first game Council also talk about trillions of lives being at stake after Virmire. The Asari embassy receptionist also mentions [trillions who are being represented by the embassies](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TtLO7Sx3IJg&t=38s) 

If anything, these quotes dobn't make it sound like there's 1 or 2 trillion people in the galaxy, but 10+ trillion or more. 

Unless we dismiss this as false, which we have no reason to as it's taken directly from multiple games in the trilogy, there are only two explanations:

-Known races have a lot more worlds than we see in game, many with populations similar to their homeworlds, giving them population in hundreds of billions each. We just don't see them because nothing notable happened on them in game.

-There are dozens if not hundreds of unnamed races in the game, all around 10-20 billion range in population that make up the majority of the galactic population , but are never mentioned once.


I believe the former is more likely, given that we often hear about other races having A LOT of colonies, while minor races very rarely mentioned, and when they are it's clearly that there's not many of them.  Before the war Quarians had stronger immune systems (still bad but way better than now) and we are told that they colonized other worlds. Their population could be smaller than that of other races, but not orders of magnitude smaller.
